name: Sink-Sink
description: Sink-Sink is a card game commonly played in Niger; a variant of Agram with five cards per player instead of six, dealt in sets of three and two. Players follow suit; the winner of each trick leads to the next. The player who wins the fifth and last trick wins the game.

rules.objective: Win the fifth and last trick to win the game. There is no point scoring; the only goal is to take the final trick.
rules.gameplay:
1. Deal: Five cards each in two batches (three then two). Player to dealer's right cuts. Play proceeds counter-clockwise.
2. Play: The player to dealer's right leads any card face up. Each player in turn must play a card of the same suit if possible; otherwise any card. Highest card of the suit led wins the trick.
3. Next trick: The winner of the trick leads any card to start the next trick.
4. Winning: After five tricks, whoever won the fifth (last) trick wins the game and deals next.
keyRules: Must follow suit when possible; otherwise any card may be played
Rank in each suit (high to low): A, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3. In spades the highest card is 10 (Ace of Spades is removed)
Winner of the last trick wins the game

strategy.basic: Follow suit when possible; try to keep high cards for the last trick.
strategy.intermediate: Track which cards have been played; count remaining cards in each suit to judge when to take the lead.
strategy.advanced: Time winning the lead so you can control the last trick; avoid wasting high cards early.
tips: Winning the fifth trick is the only goal; earlier tricks matter only for positioning.
